q-35626.name: Question 1
q-35626.problem:
From top to bottom, fill in the blanks and hence complete the proof of the following statement using the axioms $[\text{A}1]-[\text{A}8]$ given below.

*Statement:*

*If $w$ is a vector such that $x+w=x$ for some $x\in V$, then $w=0.$*

*Proof:*

$$
\begin{aligned}x+w & =x &  & [\,\text{given}\,] \\ (x+w)+(-x) & =x+(-x) &  & [\,\text{add }-x\text{ to both sides}\,] \\ (w+x)+(-x) & =x+(-x) &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,] \\ w+(x+(-x)) & =x+(-x) &  & [\,\text{axiom A2}\,] \\ w+0 & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A4}\,] \\ w & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,]\end{aligned}
$$

The axioms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{[A1]}:x+y=y+x & \text{[A5]}:1\cdot x=x \\ \text{[A2]}:(x+y)+z=x+(y+z) & \text{[A6]}:\alpha (\beta x)=(\alpha \beta )x \\ \text{[A3]}:x+0=x & \text{[A7]}:(\alpha +\beta )x=\alpha x+\beta x \\ \text{[A4]}:x+(-x)=0 & \text{[A8]}:\alpha (x+y)=\alpha x+\alpha y\end{aligned}
$$
q-35626.worked_solution:
Using the vector space axioms, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+w & =x &  & [\,\text{given}\,] \\ (x+w)+(-x) & =x+(-x) &  & [\,\text{add }-x\text{ to both sides}\,] \\ (w+x)+(-x) & =x+(-x) &  & [\,\text{axiom }\text{A1}\,] \\ w+(x+(-x)) & =x+(-x) &  & [\,\text{axiom A2}\,] \\ w+0 & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A4}\,] \\ w & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom }\text{A3}\,]\end{aligned}
$$

q-35640.name: Question 2
q-35640.problem:
Let $T$ be the set of all $2\times 2$ matrices $({a}_{ij})$  with real entries, such that  ${a}_{11}+{a}_{22}$ is rational.  Complete the following sentence:

*$T$ is **not** a vector space (with respect to addition of matrices and multiplication of matrices by a real number) because $\text{____}\,.$*
q-35640.worked_solution:
The correct answer is 

*$T$ is **not** a vector space (with respect to addition of matrices and multiplication of matrices by a real number) because **multiplication by a scalar is not closed.** *

 For example, the identity matrix 

$$
I=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

lies in $T$, but

$$
\sqrt{2}\cdot I=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]\notin T
$$

because $\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{2}$ is not a rational number.

On the other hand,

- The zero matrix belongs to $T.$  $\,✓$

- Addition of matrices with real entries is commutative, in general.    $\,✓$

- Addition of matrices with real entries is associative, in general.    $\,✓$

- Given any $A\in T,$  the additive inverse matrix $-A=(-1)\cdot A$ is also in  $T,$ and   $A+(-A)=O.$  $\,✓$

Question 2
?

Let T be the set of all 2×2 matrices (aij) with real entries, such that a11+a22 is rational. Complete the following sentence:

T is not a vector space (with respect to addition of matrices and multiplication of matrices by a real number) because ____.

a
there exists a matrix A∈T such that A+B≠O for any B∈T.
b
T does not contain the zero matrix O
c
addition of matrices in T is not associative
d
addition of matrices in T is not commutative
e
multiplication by a scalar is not closed
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The correct answer is

T is not a vector space (with respect to addition of matrices and multiplication of matrices by a real number) because multiplication by a scalar is not closed.

For example, the identity matrix I=[1001], lies in T, but 2⋅I=[2002]∉T because 2+2 is not a rational number.

On the other hand,

  • The zero matrix belongs to T. ✓

  • Addition of matrices with real entries is commutative, in general. ✓

  • Addition of matrices with real entries is associative, in general. ✓

  • Given any A∈T, the additive inverse matrix −A=(−1)⋅A is also in T, and A+(−A)=O. ✓

q-94792.name: Question 3
q-94792.problem:
Let $A$ be the set of all functions $f:R\to R$ of the form  $f(x)=a+{x}^{2},$ where $a\in R.$ Complete the following sentence:

*$A$ is **not** a vector space (with respect to function addition and scalar multiplication) because $\text{_________}\,.$*
q-94792.worked_solution:
The correct answer is as follows:

*$A$ is **not** a vector space (with respect to function addition and scalar multiplication) because **multiplication of $f\in A$ by a scalar is not closed.** *

For example, if $\alpha =2$ and $f(x)={x}^{2},$ then $\alpha f(x)=2{x}^{2}.$ So, $\alpha f(x)\notin A$ because the coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ is not $1.$

On the other hand:

- Addition of real valued functions  is associative. $\,✓$

- Addition and scalar multiplication of polynomials satisfy the distributive laws.
$\,✓$

- Addition of real valued functions  is commutative. $\,✓$

- $1\cdot f=f$ for all $f\in A.$ $\,✓$

q-94807.name: Question 4
q-94807.problem:
Let $K$ be the set of all $2\times 1$ matrices $[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],$ such that $x,y\in R$ and $x+y=1.$  Complete the following sentence:

*$K$ is **not** a vector space (with respect to matrix addition and scalar multiplication) because $\text{_________}\,.$*
q-94807.worked_solution:
The correct answer is as follows:

*$K$ is **not** a vector space (with respect to matrix addition and scalar multiplication) because **the $2\times 1$  zero matrix does not belong to $K.$** *  

Indeed, adding the entries of the $2\times 1$  zero matrix yields $0+0=0\ne 1.$

On the other hand:

- addition of matrices is associative. $\,✓$

- Addition of matrices  is commutative. $\,✓$

q-94807.html:
Question 4
?

Let K be the set of all 2×1 matrices [xy], such that x,y∈R and x+y=1. Complete the following sentence:

K is not a vector space (with respect to matrix addition and scalar multiplication) because _________.

a
 1⋅A≠A for all A∈K
b
the 2×1 zero matrix does not belong to K
c
addition of matrices is not commutative
d
addition of matrices is not associative
e
addition and scalar multiplication of matrices do not satisfy the distributive laws
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The correct answer is as follows:

K is not a vector space (with respect to matrix addition and scalar multiplication) because the 2×1 zero matrix does not belong to K.

Indeed, adding the entries of the 2×1 zero matrix yields 0+0=0≠1.

On the other hand:

  • addition of matrices is associative. ✓

  • addition and scalar multiplication of matrices satisfy the distributive laws. ✓

  • Addition of matrices is commutative. ✓

  • 1⋅A=A for all A∈K. ✓

q-106939.problem:
From top to bottom, fill in the blanks and hence complete the proof of the following statement using the axioms $[\text{A}1]-[\text{A}8]$ given below.

*Statement:*

*If $w$ and $v$ are vectors such that $x+w=v+x$ for some $x\in V$, then $w=v.$*

*Proof:*

$$
\begin{aligned}x+w & =v+x &  & [\,\text{given}\,] \\ (x+w)+(-x) & =(v+x)+(-x) &  & [\,\text{add }-x\text{ to both sides}\,] \\ (w+x)+(-x) & =(v+x)+(-x) &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,] \\ w+(x+(-x)) & =v+(x+(-x)) &  & [\,\text{axiom A2}\,] \\ w+0 & =v+0 &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,] \\ w & =v &  & [\,\text{axiom A3}\,]\end{aligned}
$$

The axioms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{[A1]}:x+y=y+x & \text{[A5]}:1\cdot x=x \\ \text{[A2]}:(x+y)+z=x+(y+z) & \text{[A6]}:\alpha (\beta x)=(\alpha \beta )x \\ \text{[A3]}:x+0=x & \text{[A7]}:(\alpha +\beta )x=\alpha x+\beta x \\ \text{[A4]}:x+(-x)=0 & \text{[A8]}:\alpha (x+y)=\alpha x+\alpha y\end{aligned}
$$
q-106939.worked_solution:
Using the vector space axioms, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+w & =v+x &  & [\,\text{given}\,] \\ (x+w)+(-x) & =(v+x)+(-x) &  & [\,\text{add }-x\text{ to both sides}\,] \\ (w+x)+(-x) & =(v+x)+(-x) &  & [\,\text{axiom }\text{A1}\,] \\ w+(x+(-x)) & =v+(x+(-x)) &  & [\,\text{axiom A2}\,] \\ w+0 & =v+0 &  & [\,\text{axiom }\text{A4}\,] \\ w & =v &  & [\,\text{axiom A3}\,]\end{aligned}
$$
